Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mizu (development version)

Initial release.

  • mizu_channel(): lock-free SPSC channels between R processes — or between R and a Python peer — over POSIX shared memory or Win32 file mappings, with batching, serialization-free raw tiers, sentinel outcomes for a full ring, timeout, close or peer death, and peer death delivered as an OS event.
  • mizu_pool(): work-stealing task pools over spawned workers — mizu_submit() / mizu_collect(), batch submission, mizu_collect_any() / mizu_collect_all(), worker retirement and respawn, nested submission from inside a task, and classed remote errors transported with their fields intact.
  • mizu_map(): a parallel map over one shared staging region — adaptive morsel scheduling, streaming and prepared maps, .template output areas with a zero-copy .collect = "view", and reproducible per-element random streams (.seed).
  • Zero-copy vectors and data frames — received as ALTREP views over the shared pages, and a view sent on again crosses by reference.
  • Zero-copy Arrow interchange — ‘arrow’ tables and record batches travel as one shared-memory frame, converting back with mizu_as_arrow() without copying.
  • Python interop — channels and pools mix with Python processes running pymizu: mizu_py_launcher() spawns peers and workers, and mizu_call() task specs drive them, data frames crossing with full type fidelity.
  • Event-driven async — mizu_recv_async(), mizu_recv_handler(), and as.promise() methods for channels, tasks, and maps over later and promises, ready for Shiny.
  • Housekeeping — mizu_prune() reclaims shared memory orphaned by dead processes; mizu_pool_dump() introspects a running or hung pool.
